---
title: "Branches & Pull Requests"
---

## Why branches?

So far, all work has gone directly onto `main` — the live version of the code. That works fine alone. With collaborators, it creates problems:

- ❌ Two people editing the same file at the same time creates conflicts
- ❌ Half-finished changes can break the code for everyone
- ❌ No way to review work before it goes live

::: {.callout-note}
A **branch** is a safe copy of the code where you can make changes without affecting `main` — until you are ready.
:::

![](images/branching.png){fig-align="center" height="220"}

::: {.callout-important}
`main` stays clean and stable at all times by keeping work on branches.
:::

## Pull requests

When your branch is ready, you open a **pull request** (PR) — a request to merge your changes into `main`.

A PR lets your teammates:

- See exactly what changed, line by line
- Leave comments on specific lines
- Approve the changes — or ask for revisions
- Merge once everyone is happy

::: {.callout-tip}
One issue → one branch → one PR. Small, focused changes are much easier to review than one enormous commit.
:::

## Creating a branch & opening a PR

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Python (VSCode)

1. Click the branch name in the bottom-left status bar
2. Select **Create new branch** — name it `fix/issue-number-short-description`
3. Make your changes and commit as normal
4. Click **Publish Branch** in the Source Control tab
5. VSCode will prompt you to **Create Pull Request** — click it
6. Add a title, link to the issue (type `#` to search), and click **Create**

### R (RStudio)

1. In the **Git tab**, click the branch icon 🔀
2. Click **New Branch** — name it `fix/issue-number-short-description`
3. Make your changes and commit as normal
4. Click **Push** (↑) to push your branch to GitHub
5. GitHub will show a banner: **"Compare & pull request"** — click it
6. Add a title, link to the issue (type `#` to search), and click **Create pull request**

:::

## Reviewing & merging a PR

1. Open the repository on GitHub
2. Click the **Pull requests** tab
3. Open the PR you have been assigned to review
4. Click **Files changed** to see the diff
5. Click `+` next to any line to leave a comment
6. When done, click **Review changes** and choose:
   - ✅ **Approve** — looks good, ready to merge
   - 💬 **Comment** — feedback but no verdict yet
   - ❌ **Request changes** — needs fixes before merging
7. Once approved → click **Merge pull request**

## In practice

::: {.callout-caution}
### Exercises

3.5 Assign yourself to an open issue

3.6 Create a branch, make your changes, commit then push

3.7 Open a pull request — link it to the issue and assign a teammate as reviewer

3.8 Review a teammate's PR — leave at least one comment, then approve

3.9 Merge the approved PR and watch the live update!
:::

## Quick reference

| Action | Where |
|---|---|
| Add a collaborator | Settings → Collaborators → Add people |
| Create an issue | Issues tab → New issue → add label + assignee |
| Create a branch (VSCode) | Click branch name in status bar → New branch |
| Create a branch (RStudio) | Git tab → branch icon 🔀 → New Branch |
| Open a pull request | Push branch → GitHub banner → Compare & pull request |
| Link PR to an issue | Type `#issue-number` in the PR description |
| Review a PR | Pull requests tab → Files changed → Review changes |
| Merge a PR | Approve → Merge pull request → Confirm |
